ctx.x: Looking back now, I think that Willie Lewis's orchestra must have been really quite good. It was quite a swinging band and had it been transported, for instance, to the Savoy, I think that Willie would have done as well as Teddy Hill, when he was there. Willie didn't have any big names but he had good musicians in the band. Big Boy Goodie could swing, and on a good night, Jack Butler could too. Billy Burns was not a great trombone player, but a lot of bands had trombone players who were not great jazzmen. The…

Jimmy Donaghue, Barbara Houtton's brother, also used to hang out with the orchestra. If we would go to a cafe after work, he would often come along. I don't know how interested in jazz he was, but he certainly seemed interested in the band.

The 3rd of July, I had another concert at the Ecole Normale de Musique. Alberta Hunter, the blues singer, Garland Wilson, a pianist-singer, and Chittison with the orchestra of Christian Wagner were the other participants, and the place was packed to standing room only. Alberta Hunter had been in Europe for quite some time but Garland Wilson, who was not a real jazz pianist, played an exciting entertainers type of piano and had not been in France very long.
